# Results — Study 473 (Balance of Power)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **smoothed
Balance of Power leads price: when buyers take over (smoothed BOP crosses up through zero), a
rise follows** — encoded as a mechanical rule. BOP = (close − open) / (high − low), smoothed
with a 14-day MA; a long fires when smoothed BOP crosses up through zero, entered at the **next
close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **1631** mechanical smoothed-BOP up-crosses pooled across the 5 tapes (smooth = 14) |
| Timing / costs | smoothed BOP is a trailing 14-day MA (causal); up-cross read on close of *t*, enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per cross |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument trend study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — smoothed-BOP up-cross vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch cross-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = cross − random.

| horizon | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 1626 | +17.8 bps | 57% | +2.37 | +13.9 bps | **+3.9 bps** | +15.8 bps | +0.42 | 0.678 |
| 10-day | 1626 | +39.8 bps | 59% | +3.57 | +36.5 bps | **+3.2 bps** | +37.8 bps | +0.26 | 0.798 |
| 20-day | 1624 | +73.9 bps | 59% | +4.08 | +81.8 bps | **−7.9 bps** | +71.9 bps | −0.43 | 0.666 |
| 60-day | 1617 | +273.7 bps | 68% | +6.13 | +306.3 bps | **−32.6 bps** | +271.7 bps | −1.08 | 0.281 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+4.08** at 20 days,
**+6.13** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the BOP up-cross is a
near-perfect dead heat — a hair ahead at 5/10 days (+3.9 / +3.2 bps) and *behind* at 20/60 days
(−7.9 / −32.6 bps). The cross-minus-random difference **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar**
(max Welch *t* = +0.42 at 5 days, *p* = 0.678). Smoothed BOP does not lead price.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent cross-sectional edge

| ticker | entries | cross | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 304 | +23.6 bps | +0.61 | +105.4 bps | **−81.8 bps** |
| QQQ | 320 | +104.2 bps | +2.84 | +130.5 bps | **−26.4 bps** |
| IWM | 382 | +66.2 bps | +1.51 | +6.1 bps | **+60.1 bps** |
| DIA | 316 | +55.2 bps | +1.69 | +65.9 bps | **−10.7 bps** |
| GLD | 309 | +120.6 bps | +3.12 | +118.3 bps | **+2.3 bps** |

Only **IWM** shows a meaningful positive delta (+60.1 bps), driven by its *weak* random baseline
(small-caps' choppier path), while SPY is −81.8 bps *behind* random. The sign flips name to name
— the hallmark of relabelled drift, not a forecasting signal.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the BOP ordering, nothing changes

The decisive "does the BOP series' ordering matter?" test: keep the per-bar BOP **marginal**
(same set of body-balance values) but permute their **sequence** before smoothing, so the
smoothed series and its zero-crosses become temporally meaningless. If smoothed BOP genuinely
led price, the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed BOP-cross 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY sign-scramble BOP | +23.6 bps | **0.994** | 500 |

**99% of scrambled-ordering BOP series match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.994). The BOP
sequence carries no information — a temporally shuffled BOP does just as well (in fact the real
one sits in the *bottom* of the cloud). "Smoothed BOP leads price" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real lead

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* BOP-leads-price structure (knob `edge`: next-day drift
follows the recent smoothed body balance), the same up-cross rule behaves exactly as it must —
so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no lead) | 238 | +5.7 bps | 50% | +0.14 |
| **1.50** (real planted lead) | 129 | +281.7 bps | 69% | **+3.19** |

With no planted lead the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (50% win — no false positive); a real planted
lead lights up at *t* = +3.19 with a 69% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The smoothed-BOP up-cross does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (cross − random = +3.9 / +3.2 / −7.9 / −32.6 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the cross-vs-random Welch
  *t* never clears 2, max +0.42 at 5 days, *p* = 0.678). The impressive one-sample *t*'s (20-day
  +4.08, 60-day +6.13) are pure beta — the upward drift of long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more fully
  by holding the index; the BOP rule trades less and pays costs on each cross, dominating nothing.
  No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Does buyer/seller balance forecast"? — BUSTED.** The sign-scramble placebo leaves the result
  intact (*p* = 0.994): temporally shuffled BOP series do as well as the real one, so the specific
  buyer/seller sequence carries no forecasting information. Balance of Power is a descriptive
  read-out of the current bar, not a lead on the next one.
